Subject: Private offer for evaluation - pricing / term options / buyer approvals

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team at Acme Cloud Services is interested in running a 6-8 week pilot for our internal developer tools using Redwood's hosted inference. Before we lock dates we need to understand a few items so we can get internal approvals: 

- Typical private offer pricing ranges for a pilot (12mo vs 36mo listing vs short-term eval pricing).
- Whether we can do a 12-month private offer with a trial/credit period in month 1.
- What approvals are required on our side (procurement thresholds / signoff levels) and on the AWS side for co-sell crediting.

Can you send a short outline of options and a mutual action plan we can share with procurement? Ideally we want something we can route to our procurement lead this week.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud Services

Subject: Re: Private offer for evaluation - pricing / term options / buyer approvals

Hi Alicia — great to hear. Appreciate the clarity on timelines. High level answers below and I've attached a one‑page MOP template you can pass to procurement (attached).

Quick answers:
- Pricing: For pilots we typically propose either a 12‑month private offer with a front‑loaded credit (month 1 or first N tokens free/discounted) or a 36‑month private offer with stepped discounts (year 1/2/3). Example ranges: $0.12–$0.18/token-equivalent for standard hosted models at pilot scale; longer tenors ~15–25% lower effective unit price depending on commit. (We will finalize after we review your usage profile.)
- Trial window: Yes — we can structure the private offer to include a 30-day credit period. That is implemented as a line-item credit in the private offer and noted in the PO.
- Approvals: On the buyer side, procurement needs PO authority and signature; if the PO exceeds your delegated approval limit it will require VP Legal signoff — we can help map thresholds. On the AWS side, co-sell crediting requires the deal to be registered with your AWS AM prior to close and some seller onboarding steps (see Vivek's note below).

Next steps I propose:
1) Vivek to share the AWS marketplace private offer checklist (seller-side) and co-sell registration steps.
2) We prepare two simple SKUs/pricing scenarios (12mo w/30d credit, 36mo stepped).
3) Acme procurement reviews MOP template and returns any procurement questions.
4) We jointly route to your AWS AM for co-sell registration once pricing is agreed.

I'll follow with the SKUs by tomorrow.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: AWS private offer checklist + co-sell routing notes

Hi all — quick note from the marketplace/partner side so we have the right sequence: 

1) AWS AM registration: Need the AWS AM to register the opportunity (AM name + AWS account ID). Without registration, co-sell crediting cannot be guaranteed.
2) Private offer docs: Seller must create the private offer in AWS Seller Central and include (a) SKU mapping, (b) pricing tiers, (c) contract term, (d) any credit line items.
3) Buyer approvals: Many enterprise buyers need PO value + term confirmed to use their delegated purchaser. If PO > $250k it often requires executive procurement signoff. 
4) Invoicing: AWS private offers can be invoiced via AWS (Marketplace) or direct (seller invoice). For co-sell we prefer Marketplace invoicing so the deal is visible to AWS for crediting.
5) Time-to-approve: Typical buyer approval routing ranges from 3 business days (small PO) to 3 weeks (multi-division committees). Plan accordingly.

I'll attach our seller-side checklist and a short template to help your AM register. Once Alicia confirms the AM name and account ID we can start the registration and I will create the private offer draft.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi / Vivek,

Thanks — procurement here. A few clarification questions before we escalate to our approval board: 

1) If we choose Marketplace invoicing, how does Redwood handle tax and remittance? Do we receive a single invoice from AWS Marketplace or do you also send a seller invoice?
2) For the 12‑month private offer with a 30‑day credit, how is the credit reflected on our PO and the Marketplace order? We need language that maps the credit to a line item for auditing.
3) We will need a standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and SOC2 evidence. We have the SOC2 checklist ready — can you confirm the latest report date?

Please see attached procurement questions (spreadsheet). We'd like to route answers + a final MOP to our legal and then schedule a DocuSign routing for signature.

Procurement Team
Acme Cloud Services

- Kimberly: upload SOC2 and DPA to the HubSpot deal and confirm legal stamping language.

I'll create a one‑page MOP with the procurement language required to map credits to PO line items. Once we have agreement we'll route to DocuSign. CC'ing AWS marketplace address to help with co-sell tracking.
